````text
# PR #4916: Patch: the lethal solver keeps to the allowance its caller gave on a board that is not wide, where a floor meant for wide boards now raises it to 60 nodes

Closes #4802

## What changed

The lethal solver now stays within the nodes its caller gave it on a normal-width board, and no `SearchBudget` field can overflow any more.

- **`scaled_budget`** (`crates/ai/src/decide.rs`):
  - On a state at or under `AI_SEARCH.fat_reference`, it now returns the caller's own budget. The solver's allowance is only capped at `nodes`; the 60-node `fat_min_lethal` floor is no longer applied there.
  - On a wide ("fat") state, both floors (`fat_min_nodes` 150, `fat_min_lethal` 60) still hold the scaled figures up, but never above the caller's own `nodes` and `lethal_nodes`.
  - The solver's share uses `saturating_mul`. The old `lethal_nodes == 0` special case is gone, because `.min(budget.lethal_nodes)` already keeps 0 at 0.
- **Saturating arithmetic** at the remaining overflow sites:
  - in `plan`: `other_worlds`, `per_finalist`, `reserve`, the `shortlist_lines` count and the `payoff_score` keep;
  - in `crates/ai/src/search.rs`: `ReplayFill::ceiling`.
  - The issue's `decide.rs:626` site was already removed by R4801000.
- **Docs:** the comments on `AiSearch.fat_min_nodes` and `fat_min_lethal` now say the floors never raise the caller's figures. Values are unchanged.
- **Spec:**
  - `spec/rulings/R4802000.md`, proven in `crates/ai/src/decide.rs` and `crates/ai/tests/ai/budget.rs`;
  - its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/4802.md`;
  - one sentence in §9.9's **Budgets.** bullet.

### What moves and what does not

- **`AI_BUDGET` and `AI_GATE_BUDGET` decide node for node as before on every state.** So do the other shipped budgets that search: `BOT_STRENGTHS[1..=4]` and `DUOS_AI_BUDGET`. Each gives the whole search at least 150 nodes and the solver at least 60, so every new `.min` is inactive and every saturating operation computes the same value. The gate smoke reads exactly what the planner's prototype read (below).
- **The weakest ladder strength keeps `lethal_nodes: 40`, and its rating needs no recalibration.** At `skill: 0.0`, `plays_best` returns false without a draw (`crates/ai/src/skill.rs`). So `crates/shared/src/bots/decide.rs` and `crates/server/src/bots/calibrate.rs` never search with its budget, and the skill miss never reads the budget. Its play and `BOT_SEED_RATINGS` do not change.
- **Test and tool budgets below the floors now spend the figures they state.** This covers `TEST_BUDGET` 150/40, `FEW`, `QUICK` 30/10 and the tutorial's 60/20. Their suites are green (below). The `nodes: 0` starved budgets in `selfplay.rs`, `fork_screen.rs` and `arena.rs` still fall back as their tests expect.

## How I tested it

**The new tests fail without the fix.** I put the old `decide.rs` and `search.rs` code back and kept the new tests. All seven failed with the issue's messages:
- `the solver spent 60`
- `lethal_nodes 10 of 1200: the solver spent 60`
- `7 of 30 nodes were the solver's, yet the beam searched no line`
- the overflow test listed `max_depth`, `finalists`, `branching` and `lethal_nodes` with `attempt to add/multiply with overflow`. `root_branching` no longer overflowed even before the fix, thanks to R4801000.

With the fix restored, I ran:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib r4802000` | 3 passed |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai budget::` | 7 passed (4 new) |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai --test ai_slow` | 69 / 1063 / 104 passed (15 daily ignored) |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-shared --features jackioh-engine/testkit` | exit 0; 331 and 682 passed in its main binaries |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server --features jackioh-engine/testkit bots::` | 98 passed |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --features jackioh-engine/testkit --bin jackioh` | 628 passed, 25 ignored (daily) |
| `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --features jackioh-engine/testkit --test acceptance` | 58 passed |
| `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm exec vitest run --project web apps/web/src/tutorial/scripts -t "random moves"` | 5 files, 5 passed (35 skipped by `-t`) |
| `cargo fmt --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo jackioh spec check` | `2589 rulings, 6403 proofs, 78296 citations in 5027 files, 35347 links: ok` |

`cargo jackioh gate` (smoke) exited 0:
```
[gate ai-vs-random] 20 wins and 0 turn-cap draws of 20; 19 wins needed; 0 search panics (220.6s)
[gate ai-vs-greedy] 17 wins and 0 turn-cap draws of 20; 14 wins needed; 0 search panics (92.6s)
[gate hard-vs-easy] 18 wins and 0 turn-cap draws of 20; 15 wins needed; 0 search panics (268.1s)
```
These are the planner's numbers exactly. The perf lines are slow because the tools suite was running alongside it on 4 cores.

I did not run the whole-workspace `cargo test` or `cargo clippy --workspace`; the harness runs both next.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **The weakest strength's `lethal_nodes` stays at 40.** The issue offered two options: recalibrate the bot, or set the constant to 60 so it says what runs. I did neither, because that budget never searches at skill 0 (above). Setting it to 60 would make the constant record a floor that no longer applies. The ruling records this as rejected.
- **The solver's share saturates rather than using 128-bit arithmetic.** It is only inexact when `lethal_nodes × scaled nodes` would pass `usize::MAX`, and the `.min`s still keep it bounded. Every other bound here saturates too.
- **Small departures from the plan:**
  - The three unit tests sit after `decide.rs`'s `LOBBYIST`/`MENACE`/`VANILLA` constants rather than between `HUMAN` and `LOBBYIST`, so that group of constants stays together.
  - `ReplayFill::ceiling`'s doc gets a one-line R4802000 note.

## Worth a second look

- **#4788 is not on this base.** Whichever of the two lands second must rebase on the other. On that rebase, #4788's `scaled.nodes + (reach - scaled.lethal_nodes)` and `budget.nodes + extended` must become `saturating_add`, or `r4802000_a_budget_field_at_its_largest_value_does_not_overflow` fails.
- **No patch fragment.** The change ships no card data; it is an AI change.
````

**Issue #4802 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #4802: Patch: the lethal solver keeps to the allowance its caller gave on a board that is not wide, where a floor meant for wide boards now raises it to 60 nodes
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

`scaled_budget` (`crates/ai/src/decide.rs:278-300`) floors the lethal solver's allowance at `AI_SEARCH.fat_min_lethal` (60) on every state, not only on a wide ("fat") one whose budget it scaled down:

```rust
let lethal_nodes = if budget.lethal_nodes == 0 { 0 } else {
    (budget.lethal_nodes * nodes / budget.nodes.max(1))
        .max(AI_SEARCH.fat_min_lethal.max(0) as usize)
        .min(nodes)
};
```

On a state that is not fat, `nodes == budget.nodes`, so the first term is the caller's own figure and the `.max(60)` raises any allowance below 60.

- The weakest ladder bot's shipped budget (`BOT_STRENGTHS[0]`, `crates/shared/src/config.rs`: 150 nodes, 40 for the solver) spends 60 of its 150 on the solver, and gains a best-first pass its 40-node allowance was never meant to reach (`lethal_quick_nodes` is 40).
- `AI_BUDGET` with `lethal_nodes: 10`: the solver spends 60.
- `{ nodes: 30, lethal_nodes: 7 }`: the solver takes all 30 and the decision is `Fallback endTurn` with 0 lines, stopped by Budget. The same 30 nodes with `lethal_nodes: 0` search 11 lines.
- The test and tool budgets below 60 are hit the same way (`skill.rs` tests' 60/15, `dev_run.rs` tests' 30/10, `sim_panics.rs` 120/20).

A smaller defect in the same arithmetic: a `SearchBudget` field at a huge value (`usize::MAX` for "no limit" in `max_depth`, `finalists`, `root_branching`, `branching` or `lethal_nodes`) overflows at `decide.rs:292`, `:616`, `:618`, `:626` and `search.rs:300`. With overflow checks that is a caught panic and a `Fallback endTurn` with `simPanics` 1; in the shipped build the sums wrap (a `root_branching + 1` floor of 0, an arbitrary solver allowance). No shipped budget reaches it; `SearchBudget` is plain caller data, deserialized from JSON by the WASM binding where `usize` is 32 bits.

### What should happen

- `SearchBudget.lethal_nodes` (`crates/ai/src/types.rs`): "Of `nodes`, the most the lethal solver may spend before the beam starts."
- `AiSearch.fat_min_lethal` (`crates/ai/src/config.rs`): "The least of the scaled budget the lethal solver's allowance shrinks to": a floor for a fat state's shrunk allowance, and `scaled_budget`'s own doc says the same.
- A budget field at any value must not panic or wrap: every result there is already bounded by a `.min(…)` or a counter's limit.

### How to reproduce

Four tests fail on `main` (3a83bd7), in [`crates/ai/tests/audit_decide.rs` at bf24a52](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/bf24a52273bd5c0e7d6f9c740b28a8d7cb7f2b3e/crates/ai/tests/audit_decide.rs) (branch `claude/vigilant-mayer-pmyrhr`): `lethal_nodes_caps_the_solver_on_a_state_that_is_not_fat`, `the_weakest_ladder_bots_solver_keeps_to_its_40_nodes`, `a_small_budget_still_leaves_the_beam_its_nodes`, `a_budget_field_at_its_largest_value_does_not_overflow`.

The measure they use: with `max_depth: 0` the beam takes no node, so a decision's nodes are its price probes' plus the solver's, and the probes' are what the same decision spends with `lethal_nodes: 0`. The board is 12 cards and 7 candidates, well under `fat_reference` (30), with no lethal on it.

```rust
fn solver_nodes(budget: SearchBudget) -> usize {
    let state = mid_board();
    let no_beam = SearchBudget { max_depth: 0, ..budget };
    let prices = decided(&state, SearchBudget { lethal_nodes: 0, ..no_beam }).stats.nodes;
    decided(&state, no_beam).stats.nodes - prices
}
#[test]
fn lethal_nodes_caps_the_solver_on_a_state_that_is_not_fat() {
    assert_eq!(solver_nodes(SearchBudget { lethal_nodes: 300, ..AI_BUDGET }), 300, "PREMISE: the solver spends its allowance here");
    let asked = SearchBudget { lethal_nodes: 10, ..AI_BUDGET };
    assert!(solver_nodes(asked) <= 10, "lethal_nodes 10 of 1200: the solver spent {}", solver_nodes(asked));
}
```

Output today: `lethal_nodes 10 of 1200: the solver spent 60`; `the solver spent 60` (the weakest bot); `7 of 30 nodes were the solver's, yet the beam searched no line`; and for the overflow test five entries such as `"max_depth: Fallback, Some(\"attempt to add with overflow\")"`.

### Where

The AI: `crates/ai/src/decide.rs` (`scaled_budget`, `plan`), `crates/ai/src/search.rs:300`.

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- Apply the floors only when the budget was actually scaled (`fat > reference`), and never above the caller's own figures: `.max(fat_min_lethal).min(budget.lethal_nodes)`. The same goes for `fat_min_nodes`, which raises a fat state's `nodes` to 150 even when the caller's `nodes` is smaller; the root counter still caps the spend, but `remaining` and the reserve are then worked out on nodes that do not exist.
- Use saturating arithmetic at the five overflow sites.
- At `AI_BUDGET` and `AI_GATE_BUDGET` (300 of 1,200) nothing changes on a state that is not fat, so practice and the gates play node for node as before. Say so in the pull request, with the gate smoke.
- **The weakest ladder bot moves.** `BOT_SEED_RATINGS` were calibrated on the code as it runs, with that bot's solver at 60. Restoring 40 changes it slightly. Either re-check its rating (`crates/server/tests/bots/calibrate.rs`) or, if a person prefers, set `BOT_STRENGTHS[0].lethal_nodes` to 60 so the bot plays as it does today and the constant says what runs.
- **Mind #4788** (the AI audit tracker #4787's wide-board finding), which changes how far the solver may reach past a *scaled* allowance. This issue is the other side of `scaled_budget`: the unscaled case. Whichever lands second rebases on the first.
- No test or ruling pins the floor on an unscaled budget (the only ruling on these constants is R2575000, on `fat_budget_nodes`).

Found by an audit of the AI crate; the reproduction was run and the code path read before filing.

```rust
/// The budget a decision of `fat` width spends (AI_SEARCH.fat_*). At or under fat_reference, the
/// caller's own, the lethal solver's allowance at most its `nodes`. Past it, `nodes` at most
/// `fat_budget_nodes` (R2575000), in inverse proportion to the width, floored at fat_min_nodes; the
/// lethal solver keeps its share of it, floored at fat_min_lethal. R4802000: neither floor raises a
/// figure above the caller's own, so a solver the caller gave nothing keeps nothing, and the share's
/// product saturates, so a field at any value overflows nothing. The search's shape is unchanged.
fn scaled_budget(budget: SearchBudget, fat: usize) -> SearchBudget {
    let reference = AI_SEARCH.fat_reference.max(1) as usize;
    if fat <= reference {
        return SearchBudget { lethal_nodes: budget.lethal_nodes.min(budget.nodes), ..budget };
    }
    let from = budget.nodes.min(AI_SEARCH.fat_budget_nodes.max(0) as usize);
    let nodes = (from * reference / fat)
        .max(AI_SEARCH.fat_min_nodes.max(0) as usize)
        .min(budget.nodes);
    let lethal_nodes = (budget.lethal_nodes.saturating_mul(nodes) / budget.nodes.max(1))
        .max(AI_SEARCH.fat_min_lethal.max(0) as usize)
        .min(budget.lethal_nodes)
        .min(nodes);
    SearchBudget { nodes, lethal_nodes, ..budget }
}
```

A decision on a state wider than `AI_SEARCH.fat_reference` (30) scales its budget down ([[R2575000]]), floored so the widest states still search: at least `fat_min_nodes` (150), the lethal solver's share at least `fat_min_lethal` (60). `scaled_budget` applied the solver's floor on every state, so a budget that gave the solver fewer than 60 nodes saw it spend 60 on a board of ordinary width: 60 of a 150-node budget that gave it 40, and all of a 30-node budget, whose decision then fell back to End turn with no line searched. On a fat state either floor could raise a figure past the caller's own. A field at `usize::MAX` (a caller's "no limit") overflowed the beam's reserve and the replay fill's ceiling. No Hearthstone rule is involved: the AI's use of nodes changes no game.

**The rule.** On a state at or under `fat_reference`'s width a decision spends the caller's own budget, the lethal solver at most `lethal_nodes` and never more than `nodes`. On a fat state the floors hold the scaled figures up, but never above the caller's own `nodes` and `lethal_nodes`, so a solver the caller gave nothing still runs on nothing. The scaling, the beam's reserve and the replay fill's ceiling saturate rather than overflow. Every shipped budget that searches (`AI_BUDGET`, `AI_GATE_BUDGET`, `BOT_STRENGTHS[1]` to `[4]`, the Duos AI team's) gives the solver at least 60 nodes and the whole at least 150, so it decides node for node as before on every state. The weakest ladder strength's budget, 150 nodes and 40 of them the solver's, runs only where a test raises its skill: at its skill of 0 every decision is the skill miss ([[R2214000]]), so its play and its seed rating ([[R748000]]) do not change.

**Rejected.** Raising the weakest strength's `lethal_nodes` to 60, the figure the floor ran it at: none of its decisions searches, and the constant would stand for a floor that no longer applies. Computing the solver's share in 128 bits, exact at sizes no budget reaches, where every other bound here saturates.

/// R4802000: a mid-game board well under `AI_SEARCH.fat_reference`'s width (12 cards, 7 candidates), with
/// no lethal on it.
fn narrow_board() -> GameState {
    register_cards();
    scenario(json!({
        "seed": "audit-decide-mid", "active": AI, "turn": 9,
        "p1": { "hand": ["core-008", "core-011", "core-019", "core-044"], "field": ["core-008", "core-011"],
                "mana": 5, "library": ["core-008", "core-011", "core-020"] },
        "p2": { "hand": ["core-011", "core-008"], "field": ["core-008", "core-019"],
                "library": ["core-008", "core-011", "core-020"] },
    }))
    .state()
    .clone()
}

fn decided(state: &GameState, budget: SearchBudget) -> Decision {
    decide(state, AI, &mut ai_options("audit-decide", budget)).expect("a decision")
}

/// The nodes the lethal solver spent on `narrow_board` under `budget`: with `max_depth` 0 the beam takes
/// none, so a decision's nodes are its prices' and the solver's, and the prices' are what the same
/// decision spends with `lethal_nodes` 0.
fn solver_nodes(budget: SearchBudget) -> usize {
    let state = narrow_board();
    let no_beam = SearchBudget { max_depth: 0, ..budget };
    let prices = decided(&state, SearchBudget { lethal_nodes: 0, ..no_beam }).stats.nodes;
    decided(&state, no_beam).stats.nodes - prices
}

#[test]
fn r4802000_a_budget_field_at_its_largest_value_does_not_overflow() {
    let state = narrow_board();
    let big = usize::MAX;
    let cases = [
        ("max_depth", SearchBudget { max_depth: big, ..AI_BUDGET }),
        ("finalists", SearchBudget { finalists: big, ..AI_BUDGET }),
        ("root_branching", SearchBudget { root_branching: big, ..AI_BUDGET }),
        ("branching", SearchBudget { branching: big, ..AI_BUDGET }),
        ("lethal_nodes", SearchBudget { lethal_nodes: big, ..AI_BUDGET }),
    ];
    let mut failed: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (name, budget) in cases {
        let decision = decided(&state, budget);
        if decision.stats.sim_panics > 0 {
            failed.push(format!("{name}: {:?}, {:?}", decision.reason, decision.first_sim_panic));
        }
    }
    assert!(failed.is_empty(), "{failed:#?}");

- **Hidden information and the client:** not touched.
````
